job.title: Fiduciary Services Manager
job.description:
We are recruiting for an experienced Fiduciary Services Manager on behalf of our client, a growing organisation within the professional fiduciary services sector. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated professional with experience in board support, legal services, fiduciary administration or corporate administration to join a high-performing team and develop towards a future leadership role.

In this position, you will support a diverse portfolio of complex structures, work closely with high-net-worth private clients, regulated entities and corporate groups, and deliver a professional, high-touch client service.

Company Information

Our client is part of a global, private equity-backed group providing specialist professional services to a diverse international client base. The organisation operates within a fast-paced, professional environment where accuracy, client service, collaboration and continuous development are highly valued.

You will be joining an experienced Fiduciary Services team that supports private clients, regulated entities and corporate structures. The culture is energetic, collaborative and delivery-focused, providing the opportunity for you to build your expertise while contributing to the growth and success of the team.

Responsibilities and Duties

As Fiduciary Services Manager, your responsibilities will include:

  • Supporting the administration of a portfolio of private client, regulated and corporate structures.
  • Managing client, legal adviser and intermediary relationships to ensure consistently high service standards.
  • Preparing and reviewing board minutes, resolutions and other corporate documentation.
  • Coordinating board meetings, including preparation, documentation management and follow-up actions.
  • Maintaining accurate fiduciary services records and data within ViewPoint.
  • Working closely with Compliance and Corporate Administration teams to manage annual reporting and regulatory deadlines.
  • Supporting senior team members with business development activities and client relationship management.
  • Taking ownership of assigned tasks and contributing to an efficient, professional and collaborative team environment.
  • Developing the knowledge and experience required to undertake client board appointments in the future.

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this Fiduciary Services Manager role, you will ideally have:

  • At least five years’ relevant experience in fiduciary administration, corporate administration, board support, legal services or a related professional services environment.
  • Experience supporting boards, preparing corporate documentation, or managing corporate administration processes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate confidently and professionally with clients and advisers.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines and complex structures.
  • A proactive, adaptable approach with a willingness to take ownership and deliver high-quality results.
  • Confidence working in client-facing situations, including with private clients, intermediaries and professional advisers.
  • Ambition to progress your career within fiduciary services and develop towards client board appointments or an Associate Director role.
  • Experience working with private clients, high-net-worth individuals or within the Cayman Islands regulatory environment would be advantageous.
  • Familiarity with ViewPoint would be beneficial.

Benefits and Perks

This opportunity offers the chance to join a growing, internationally connected professional services group and develop your career within fiduciary services.

Your benefits package includes:

  • 100% employer-paid premium health insurance 
  • A discretionary annual bonus
  • One remote-working day per week.
  • A clear career pathway towards progression into an Associate Director position.
  • The opportunity to work with a diverse portfolio of sophisticated clients and complex structures.

job.title: Accounts Payable Officer
job.description:
We are recruiting for an experienced Accounts Payable Officer on behalf of our client, a respected private educational organisation. This role is responsible for supporting the day-to-day accounts payable and general accounting operations, ensuring supplier payments, financial records, reporting and administrative processes are completed accurately, efficiently and in line with internal policies and accounting standards.

You will play an important role in maintaining efficient financial operations while providing a professional, customer-focused service to suppliers, parents, students, staff and other stakeholders.

Company Information

Our client is a private co-educational educational institution committed to delivering high-quality learning and supporting the development of students within a values-led environment. The organisation promotes a culture built on integrity, collaboration, accountability and service.

You will join the Finance team, working closely with the Finance Manager and supporting the wider school administration community. The successful candidate will contribute to a professional and supportive workplace where accuracy, confidentiality and strong working relationships are highly valued.

Responsibilities and Duties

As the Accounts Payable Officer, you will be responsible for:

  • Managing the day-to-day accounts payable function in accordance with financial policies, procedures and generally accepted accounting principles.
  • Setting up and maintaining supplier records while ensuring vendor information remains accurate and up to date.
  • Reviewing, verifying and processing supplier invoices, bills and statements, investigating discrepancies where required.
  • Ensuring timely and accurate payments to suppliers, as well as processing staff reimbursements and refund requests.
  • Responding professionally and promptly to queries from suppliers, parents, staff and other stakeholders regarding payments and accounts.
  • Preparing online payments and cheques with appropriate supporting documentation for authorised approval.
  • Recording financial transactions accurately in QuickBooks and the organisation’s online banking portal.
  • Reconciling supplier accounts, accounts payable ledgers, medical insurance and pension payments.
  • Preparing accounts payable reports, spreadsheets and financial statements for review by the Finance Manager.
  • Assisting with monthly payroll preparation, budgeting activities and general financial reporting.
  • Maintaining appropriate financial records, including invoices, statements, contracts, correspondence and supporting documentation.
  • Supporting inventory controls, fixed asset registers, school supply records and procurement processes.
  • Coordinating purchase orders by obtaining quotations, maintaining supplier communication and ensuring approvals are received.
  • Assisting with internal and external audit requirements while identifying and escalating any accounts payable compliance issues.

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this Accounts Payable Officer role, you will ideally have:

  • A Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
  • A minimum of three years’ experience working in accounts payable, with proven experience using QuickBooks.
  • Experience managing a high volume of invoices, supplier accounts and financial transactions.
  • Strong knowledge of general accounting principles and accounts payable practices.
  • Excellent proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Microsoft Excel.
  • Strong numerical ability with a high level of accuracy, attention to detail and organisation.
  • The ability to manage confidential financial information with professionalism, integrity and discretion.
  • Effective communication, interpersonal, negotiation and time-management skills.
  • The ability to work independently, prioritise competing demands and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • A collaborative mindset with the ability to build positive relationships across a diverse organisation.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to analyse information and recommend practical solutions.
  • A commitment to ethical conduct, accountability and maintaining high professional standards.

Benefits and Perks

This opportunity offers the chance to join a professional and purpose-driven organisation where your financial expertise will directly support the effective operation of an established educational environment.

Benefits and advantages include:

  • The opportunity to work within a respected, supportive and collaborative Finance team.
  • Exposure to a broad range of accounts payable, general accounting and procurement responsibilities.
  • A role that values accuracy, initiative, accountability and professional development.
  • Generous benefits package including discounted tuition.

job.title: Legal Secretary
job.description:
We are recruiting on behalf of our client, a leading professional services organisation, for an experienced Legal Secretary to join their Corporate team in the Cayman Islands. This is an excellent opportunity for a highly organised and detail-oriented professional to provide comprehensive administrative and secretarial support to legal professionals within a fast-paced and collaborative environment. 

Company Information

Our client is a well-established international organisation operating within the legal and professional services sector. Known for its high standards, client-focused approach, and supportive culture, the firm provides specialist services to a diverse portfolio of corporate and commercial clients. 

You will join a busy and professional Corporate team where collaboration, attention to detail, and exceptional client service are highly valued. The company invests in its people and offers opportunities to develop your skills while working alongside experienced professionals in a dynamic environment.
 

Responsibilities and Duties

As a Legal Secretary, your responsibilities will include:

  • Drafting, proofreading, and amending legal documents, reports, and correspondence.
  • Providing comprehensive secretarial and administrative support to fee earners and senior legal professionals.
  • Managing diaries, calendars, schedules, and meeting arrangements.
  • Handling internal and external telephone enquiries professionally and efficiently.
  • Maintaining and organising files, records, and legal documentation.
  • Completing company searches, conflict checks, and matter administration tasks.
  • Assisting with client events, marketing initiatives, and business development activities.
  • Supporting billing processes, invoice administration, file opening, closing, and archiving procedures. 

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this Legal Secretary position, you should have:

  • A minimum of two years' experience in a secretarial or administrative role.
  • Recent legal secretarial experience within a law firm environment.
  • Knowledge of legal terminology and legal documentation processes.
  • Excellent typing speed and accuracy, with strong document formatting skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word.
  • Experience using document management and client management systems.
  • Outstanding organisational skills with the ability to prioritise competing deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with excellent attention to detail and a collaborative approach. 

Benefits and Perks

In return for your expertise and commitment, our client offers a competitive benefits package, including:

  • Generous annual leave entitlement, with the option to buy or sell additional holiday.
  • Performance-related discretionary bonus scheme.
  • Life assurance benefit.
  • Gym membership.
  • A supportive working environment with opportunities for professional growth and development.

job.title: Temporary Transcribor/Editor Administrator
job.description:
We are recruiting on behalf of our client for a temporary Transcriber/Editor to join a respected public sector organisation. This is an excellent opportunity for a highly skilled editor, proofreader, or administrative professional to contribute to the production of official parliamentary records, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and professionalism in published reports and transcripts. The role is ideal for someone with exceptional written English skills, strong attention to detail, and a passion for research and public service.

Company Information

Our client is a well-established organisation within the government and public administration sector, dedicated to supporting parliamentary processes and maintaining official records of legislative proceedings. The organisation is recognised for its commitment to integrity, impartiality, professionalism, and public service.

You will join a collaborative team responsible for producing, editing, and publishing official transcripts and reports. Working alongside experienced professionals, you will play an important role in preserving accurate records while supporting high standards of governance and accountability. 

Responsibilities and Duties

As a Hansard Editor, you will:

  • Edit and proofread transcripts of parliamentary proceedings, committee meetings, and official hearings to ensure accuracy and consistency.
  • Listen to digital audio recordings to verify content and ensure proceedings are correctly attributed.
  • Correct spelling, grammar, punctuation, formatting, and style while maintaining the original meaning and context.
  • Conduct research to verify quotations, names, organisations, locations, and factual references.
  • Prepare, format, and distribute transcripts for review and incorporate approved amendments where required.
  • Assist with the indexing, publication, and archiving of official reports and records.
  • Maintain databases and support the production of electronic and PDF publications.
  • Undertake research and administrative tasks in support of senior stakeholders and parliamentary operations. 

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this role, you should have:

  • An Associate's degree in a relevant field with office or secretarial experience involving editing and proofreading, or significant equivalent professional experience.
  • Demonstrated experience editing, proofreading, and reviewing professional documents.
  • Excellent knowledge of English grammar, spelling, punctuation, and written comprehension.
  • Strong research, fact-checking, and information verification skills.
  • Advanced Microsoft Word and document formatting skills.
  • Accurate keyboarding and transcription abilities.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Strong communication skills, discretion, attention to detail, and the ability to work effectively within a team environment. 

Benefits and Perks

  • Competitive hourly rate.
  • Temping provides the opportunity to explore various industries and companies, allowing you to gain diverse experience and build professional connections while enjoying the flexibility of short-term roles.
  • Standard benefits as per Labour Law (vacation, pension, and health insurance).

job.title: Corporate Administrator (BO)
job.description:
An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Corporate Administrator to join a busy and growing Governance Services team within a well-established professional services organisation in the Cayman Islands. Recruiting on behalf of a respected employer in the financial services sector, this role offers the chance to support regulatory reporting, corporate administration and data management activities while developing your career within a collaborative and professional environment.

Company Information

This opportunity is with a highly regarded organisation operating within the corporate services and financial services industry. Known for delivering high-quality governance, regulatory and administration solutions, the business has built a reputation for professionalism, client service excellence and operational integrity.

You will join a supportive Governance Services team that works closely with a diverse portfolio of local and international clients. The company fosters a collaborative culture where teamwork, professional development and continuous improvement are encouraged, providing an environment where you can grow both personally and professionally.

Responsibilities and Duties

As a Corporate Administrator, you will:

  • Maintain and update beneficial ownership registers in accordance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
  • Collect, verify and accurately record beneficial ownership information from directors, shareholders, members and other stakeholders.
  • Prepare and submit beneficial ownership filings to the relevant authorities within required deadlines.
  • Maintain corporate records and databases, ensuring all information remains accurate and up to date.
  • Monitor changes in ownership structures and update records accordingly.
  • Liaise with clients and internal departments to obtain required documentation and provide status updates.
  • Support billing activities, including assisting with invoicing processes and resolving client account queries.
  • Assist with audits, due diligence requests, internal reviews and process improvement initiatives.

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this Corporate Administrator role, you should have:

  • Previous experience as a Corporate Administrator or in a similar role within a corporate services provider, law firm or financial services environment.
  • A sound understanding of corporate structures, governance processes and regulatory requirements.
  • Experience maintaining corporate records and working with corporate administration systems or databases.
  • Strong attention to detail with excellent organisational and record-keeping skills.
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and consistently meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills when working with both clients and colleagues.
  • A proactive approach with the ability to take ownership of tasks and work independently when required.
  • Experience with beneficial ownership reporting, offshore jurisdictions, Microsoft Excel, reporting tools or ViewPoint software would be advantageous.

Benefits and Perks

In return for your skills and experience, you can expect:

  • The opportunity to join a respected and growing professional services organisation.
  • Ongoing mentoring, training and professional development support.
  • Exposure to a diverse portfolio of corporate and financial services clients.
  • A collaborative, friendly and team-oriented working environment.
  • Career progression opportunities within a growing Governance Services function.
  • The chance to develop specialist knowledge in corporate administration, regulatory reporting and compliance.
  • A dynamic and fast-paced role offering varied responsibilities and continuous learning.
  • A culture that values teamwork, accuracy, client service and professional excellence.

This role is only open to Caymanian candidates. Only suitable applications will be considered and contacted.

job.title: Human Resources Manager
job.description:
We are recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Human Resources Manager to join a high-performing hospitality organisation. This is an exciting opportunity for a skilled HR professional to lead key people functions, support employee engagement, oversee recruitment and compensation activities, and drive HR initiatives that contribute to organisational success. You will work closely with senior leaders and department managers to ensure best practice across all areas of human resources.

Company Information

Our client is a well-established organisation within the luxury hospitality industry, recognised for delivering exceptional guest experiences and maintaining the highest service standards. The company fosters a culture built on professionalism, collaboration, employee development and operational excellence. 

As part of the Human Resources Leadership Team, you will join a passionate and engaged workforce that values teamwork, inclusion and continuous improvement. This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a people-focused environment where employees are encouraged to grow and succeed in their careers. 

Responsibilities and Duties

As the Human Resources Manager, your responsibilities will include:

  • Leading and overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Human Resources function. 
  • Managing recruitment activities and supporting workforce planning initiatives. 
  • Overseeing employee relations matters and promoting a positive workplace culture. 
  • Supporting compensation, benefits and HR administration processes. 
  • Coordinating training, learning and development programmes to enhance employee performance. 
  • Ensuring compliance with employment legislation, company policies and operational procedures. 
  • Partnering with managers and supervisors to provide HR guidance and ensure consistent policy application. 
  • Maintaining employee confidentiality and safeguarding sensitive HR information.

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this Human Resources Manager role, you should have:

  • A degree in Human Resources, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Previous management experience within a luxury hotel or premium hospitality environment. 
  • Experience in a Human Resources leadership position with responsibility for multiple HR functions.
  • Strong knowledge of recruitment, employee relations, compensation, training and development. 
  • Excellent organisational, planning and time-management skills. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build effective working relationships. 
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word and Excel. 
  • Experience working within multicultural environments; international recruitment experience would be advantageous. 

Benefits and Perks

In return, our client offers:

  • The opportunity to work with a respected leader in the luxury hospitality sector.
  • A collaborative and supportive working environment.
  • Ongoing training and professional development opportunities. 
  • Exposure to senior leadership and strategic HR initiatives.
  • The chance to make a meaningful impact on employee engagement and organisational culture.
  • A dynamic and diverse workplace environment. 
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package including additional benefits around travel. 
  • Long-term career growth opportunities within a people-focused organisation.

job.title: Temporary Director
job.description:
Job Summary

We are recruiting on behalf of a prominent organisation within the public and statutory sector for an Interim Director on a temporary basis for up to three months. This senior leadership opportunity is ideal for an experienced executive who can provide strategic direction, oversee day-to-day operations, and work closely with a Board to ensure the effective management of programmes, employees, finances, and stakeholder relationships.

Company Information

This opportunity is with a respected organisation operating within the public sector and statutory authority environment. The organisation plays an important role in delivering services and initiatives that support the wider community, with a strong focus on governance, accountability, and operational excellence. You will join a collaborative leadership team and work closely with Board members, senior stakeholders, and operational teams to guide the organisation through a key transitional period. 

Responsibilities and Duties

As Interim Director, you will:
  • Provide strategic and operational advice to the Board and implement approved decisions, policies, and plans. 
  • Oversee day-to-day operations, programmes, facilities, and service delivery. 
  • Establish organisational objectives, performance goals, and operational priorities.
  • Lead, develop, and support management and administrative teams. 
  • Oversee budgets, expenditure, financial reporting, and internal controls.
  • Support the preparation of budgets, financial statements, reports, and organisational records.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders, industry partners, and government entities.
  • Represent the organisation at meetings, events, committees, and official functions as required. 

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this role, you’ll ideally have:
  • A Master's degree in Business Administration and senior management experience; or a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management, Marketing, Economics, or a related field with significant management experience.
  • Strong leadership, people management, and decision-making abilities.
  • Experience managing operations, projects, budgets, assets, or multiple business functions.
  • Knowledge of business administration, financial management, human resources, procurement, governance, and organisational operations.
  • Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures, and organisational improvements.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building capabilities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and the ability to adapt to organisational systems and processes. 

Benefits and Perks

  • Competitive hourly rate.
  • Temping provides the opportunity to explore various industries and companies, allowing you to gain diverse experience and build professional connections while enjoying the flexibility of short-term roles.
  • Standard benefits as per Labour Law (vacation, pension, and health insurance).

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
We are recruiting on behalf of our client, a private family office, for an experienced Executive Assistant. This is a unique opportunity to become a trusted partner to an ultra-high-net-worth individual, providing comprehensive operational, administrative, lifestyle and travel support. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in ensuring the seamless management of personal, family and business-related matters within a highly confidential environment. 


About the Company

Our client is a private family office supporting a principal with diverse personal, philanthropic, lifestyle and business interests. Operating in a professional yet highly personalised environment, the organisation is built on trust, discretion, integrity and long-term relationships. 

You will join a small, dedicated team where collaboration, accountability and proactive problem-solving are highly valued. The role offers significant autonomy, exposure to a broad range of family office operations, and the opportunity to build a long-term career within a respected private office environment.
 

Responsibilities and Duties

As the Family Office Operations Administrator, you will:

  • Act as the primary operational support and coordination point for the Principal's personal, family and professional affairs.
  • Manage complex calendars, schedules and commitments across multiple jurisdictions and time zones.
  • Coordinate VIP international travel, including private aviation, accommodation, transport, concierge services and itinerary management. 
  • Liaise with banks, attorneys, accountants, trustees and other professional advisers while maintaining strict confidentiality. 
  • Support budgeting activities, expense tracking, financial reconciliations and reporting. 
  • Oversee property, vehicle and asset administration, ensuring licences, registrations, insurance and renewals remain up to date. 
  • Coordinate household operations, contractors, service providers and lifestyle arrangements to ensure smooth day-to-day functioning. 
  • Proactively anticipate needs, resolve issues independently and ensure tasks are completed efficiently with minimal supervision. 

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this role, you should have:

  • 5–10 years' experience supporting ultra-high-net-worth individuals, executives or within a family office environment. 
  • Strong financial and administrative experience, including expense management, reconciliations and reporting. 
  • Proven experience managing complex international travel arrangements and handling last-minute changes. 
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, along with strong digital literacy. 
  • Experience liaising with banks, legal professionals, accountants, trustees and external vendors. 
  • Excellent organisational, communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • A proactive, self-motivated approach with exceptional attention to detail and sound judgement. 
  • A valid driver's licence, a clean driving record and a demonstrated commitment to discretion, confidentiality and professionalism.


Benefits and Perks

This position offers the opportunity to join a highly respected private family office in a trusted, long-term capacity. Benefits include:

  • A rare opportunity to work closely with an ultra-high-net-worth Principal in a highly varied and rewarding role. 
  • Significant autonomy and responsibility with the ability to manage matters independently. 
  • Exposure to international family office operations, luxury asset management and VIP travel coordination. 
  • A collaborative working relationship built on trust, respect and professional integrity.
  • Diverse and engaging responsibilities across administration, travel, property, lifestyle and operational management.
  • A role where your initiative, judgement and expertise will be highly valued and trusted.

job.title: Legal Administrator
job.description:

This opportunity is with a well-established organisation operating within the legal and professional services sector. Known for its collaborative culture, high professional standards, and commitment to exceptional client service, the business offers a supportive team environment where you will work closely with legal professionals and central support colleagues. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Provide comprehensive administrative and secretarial support to legal professionals.

job.title: HR Business Partner
job.description:
Job Summary

A respected organisation within the tourism, heritage, and visitor attractions sector is seeking an experienced HR Business Partner to lead and manage all aspects of the human resources function. This is an excellent opportunity for a proactive HR professional who enjoys balancing strategic workforce planning with day-to-day HR operations. You will act as a trusted adviser to senior leaders, helping to build a positive workplace culture while ensuring compliance with employment legislation and best practice.

Company Information

Join a well-established organisation dedicated to preserving cultural, historical, and environmental assets while delivering exceptional experiences for both residents and visitors. The organisation operates several significant visitor attractions and is committed to education, sustainability, heritage preservation, and community engagement.

You will become part of a collaborative leadership team that values professionalism, accountability, continuous improvement, and employee engagement. This role offers the opportunity to influence organisational strategy while supporting teams across multiple locations.

Responsibilities & Duties

As the HR Business Partner, you will:
  • Lead the development, review, and implementation of HR policies and procedures.
  • Provide strategic HR guidance on workforce planning, talent management, employee engagement, and organisational development.
  • Manage the full recruitment and onboarding lifecycle, from job advertising to orientation.
  • Support managers with employee relations matters, including disciplinary processes, grievances, and workplace disputes.
  • Ensure compliance with employment legislation, HR policies, and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate training and development initiatives to enhance organisational capability and employee performance.
  • Oversee performance management processes, including appraisals, objective setting, and performance improvement plans.
  • Manage HR administration, including employee records, leave management, benefits administration, and payroll coordination. 
Qualifications & Skills

To be successful in this HR Business Partner role, you will have:
  • A Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
  • A minimum of 5–7 years of human resources management experience.
  • At least 3 years' experience in a supervisory, advisory, or business partnering capacity.
  • Strong knowledge of employment legislation, HR policies, and HR best practices.
  • Experience managing recruitment, employee relations, performance management, and workforce planning.
  • Proficiency in HR information systems, ideally BambooHR, and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities independently while maintaining confidentiality and professionalism.
Benefits & Perks

In return, you can expect:
  • The opportunity to play a key strategic role within a respected organisation.
  • Exposure to a diverse and dynamic multi-site working environment.
  • The chance to influence organisational culture, employee engagement, and workforce development initiatives.
  • Professional development and training opportunities.
  • Meaningful work that supports heritage, culture, tourism, and community engagement.
  • A collaborative and supportive leadership environment.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Opportunities to build relationships with senior stakeholders and contribute to organisational growth and long-term success.

job.title: Senior Client Onboarding Specialist
job.description:
We are recruiting on behalf of a leading financial services organisation for a Senior Client Onboarding Specialist to join its Corporate & Private Banking team. In this role, you will be responsible for delivering a seamless and compliant client onboarding experience, working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners. You will play a key role in ensuring all onboarding activities meet regulatory requirements while maintaining excellent client service standards.

Company Information

This opportunity is with a well-established organisation operating within the financial services and banking sector, specialising in corporate and private banking solutions.

You will be joining a collaborative and forward-thinking team where:

  • Innovation and continuous improvement are actively encouraged
  • Strong compliance and governance frameworks underpin all operations
  • Cross-functional teamwork is essential, particularly across onboarding, compliance, and relationship management
  • Career development and internal progression are supported

The business is currently undergoing a period of transformation, making it an exciting time to become part of a growing and evolving organisation.

Responsibilities and Duties

As a Senior Client Onboarding Specialist, you will be responsible for managing the end-to-end onboarding process and ensuring all regulatory and internal standards are met:

  • Review and process new client onboarding applications in line with AML/KYC requirements
  • Liaise with clients, intermediaries, and Relationship Managers to obtain and verify documentation
  • Assess client structures, business activities, and source of funds to support risk-based decisions
  • Act as a key point of coordination between business development, compliance, and internal teams
  • Ensure onboarding timelines are adhered to and service standards are consistently met
  • Monitor outstanding requirements and proactively follow up to ensure completion
  • Support periodic reviews and ongoing maintenance of existing client accounts
  • Contribute to reporting, onboarding metrics, and process improvement initiatives

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this role, you will bring strong technical knowledge alongside excellent stakeholder management and organisational skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 3–5 years’ experience in client onboarding, AML/KYC, or financial services
  • Solid understanding of AML regulations, compliance frameworks, and international financial services
  • Professional certification such as CAMS (desirable)
  • Experience working with complex client structures (corporate, trust, or offshore) preferred
  • Strong analytical skills and exceptional attention to detail
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

Benefits and Perks

This organisation offers a supportive environment where you can grow your career while contributing to meaningful work:

  • Opportunity to join a reputable and growing financial services organisation
  • Exposure to international clients and complex onboarding cases
  • Collaborative and high-performing team culture
  • Clear opportunities for career progression and development
  • Involvement in transformation and process improvement initiatives
  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package
  • Professional development support, including certifications
  • Stable, full-time employment in a regulated and respected industry

job.title: Private Banking Officer
job.description:
We are recruiting on behalf of a leading financial services organisation for a Corporate & Private Banking Officer to join their growing team in Grand Cayman. In this client-facing role, you will manage and develop relationships with corporate, high-net-worth, and institutional clients, delivering tailored banking solutions and exceptional service. You will play a key part in both relationship management and business development, supporting clients across a broad range of banking products.

Company Information

Our client is a well-established and forward-thinking financial services provider operating within the banking sector. Known for its commitment to innovation and operational excellence, the organisation is currently undergoing an exciting period of transformation and growth.

You will be joining a collaborative, high-performing team that values professionalism, client service, and continuous improvement. The culture encourages initiative, rewards strong performance, and supports career development within a dynamic and client-focused environment.

Responsibilities and Duties

As a Corporate & Private Banking Officer, your responsibilities will include:

  • Managing the opening, maintenance, and closure of client accounts, ensuring a seamless banking experience
  • Providing relationship management support to corporate, VIP, and institutional clients
  • Administering fixed deposit products, including placements, renewals, and cancellations
  • Promoting and advising on banking products such as savings accounts, deposits, and card services
  • Conducting client meetings, handling enquiries, and delivering excellent customer service
  • Identifying and developing new business opportunities to grow client portfolios
  • Representing the organisation at presentations, networking events, and industry seminars
  • Maintaining accurate client records and ensuring compliance with regulatory and internal policies

Qualifications and Skills

To be successful in this banking role, you should have:
